skill.name: Command Development
skill.description: Create and refine Claude Code slash commands with frontmatter, arguments, file references, Bash context, plugin resources, and testing guidance.
skill.summary: Build reusable Claude Code slash commands for project, personal, and plugin workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-heavy and many static hits are Markdown examples, paths, URLs, or testing snippets rather than hidden execution. However, several examples intentionally teach inline Bash commands with broad Bash access and direct slash-command argument interpolation, which creates real command-injection and over-permission risks if copied into shared commands.

remediation.issue: Inline Bash examples interpolate slash-command arguments directly.
remediation.suggestion: Show safe validation before Bash execution, quote generated values, and prefer passing arguments through scripts with strict allowlists.
Replace wildcard Bash grants with specific filters such as Bash(git:*), Bash(npm:*), or Bash(test:*).

remediation.issue: Plugin script examples run bundled scripts without trust guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to review plugin scripts, use least privilege, and document side effects before publishing commands.

remediation.issue: Deployment and release examples can affect external systems.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, environment allowlists, dry-run modes, and rollback documentation for deploy commands.

medium_findings.title: Broad Bash Permissions in Reusable Command Templates
medium_findings.description: Multiple reusable examples grant Bash(*) to commands intended for distribution. This allows broad shell execution when narrower command filters would reduce impact.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The locations explicitly show wildcard Bash access in templates. The skill also recommends narrower filters elsewhere, so this is a documentation-quality security issue rather than hidden malware.

content.value_statement: Teams need reusable commands that behave consistently across projects. This skill guides command structure, frontmatter, arguments, Bash context, plugin resources, testing, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code slash command file structure and supported command locations.
Shows how to use YAML frontmatter fields such as description, model, and allowed-tools.
Demonstrates dynamic arguments, positional parameters, and file references in commands.
Documents inline Bash context gathering and plugin resource access patterns.
Provides examples for project commands, personal commands, and plugin command workflows.
Includes testing, validation, documentation, and marketplace readiness guidance.
limitations: Does not create a runtime command engine or execute commands by itself.
Some examples require careful security review before use in shared environments.
Claude Code feature behavior may vary across installed versions.
Plugin examples assume supporting scripts, agents, skills, or templates exist.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Create shared project commands for reviews, testing, documentation, and release checks.

use_cases.title: Create Plugin Commands
use_cases.description: Design plugin commands that use plugin resources, scripts, agents, skills, and templates.

use_cases.title: Improve Personal Automation
use_cases.description: Build personal slash commands for repeated development tasks across many repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code slash command for reviewing changed files. Include a short description and clear instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Arguments and Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a slash command that accepts one file path argument, reads that file, and produces documentation for it.

prompt_templates.title: Use Safe Bash Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a command that gathers Git status before analysis. Use the narrowest allowed-tools value and explain any Bash usage.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Plugin Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plugin slash command that validates arguments, reads a plugin template, runs a plugin script, and reports failures safely.

output_examples.input: User asks for a simple code review slash command.
output_examples.output: A concise command design with description, read-only tool access, review checklist, and expected feedback format.

output_examples.input: User asks for a plugin command that runs a quality checker.
output_examples.output: A plugin command plan that references plugin resources, narrows Bash access, validates inputs, and summarizes checker output.

output_examples.input: User asks how to prepare a command for marketplace distribution.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering naming, portability, dependencies, examples, testing steps, and security review points.

best_practices: Use the narrowest allowed-tools setting that supports the command.
Validate and document every user-supplied argument before using it.
Test commands with missing, invalid, long, and unusual inputs.
anti_patterns: Do not grant Bash(*) when a specific command filter is enough.
Do not pass slash command arguments directly into shell commands without validation.
Do not hardcode personal plugin paths or local machine paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Claude Code slash commands for project, personal, and plugin workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill execute shell commands itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents command patterns that may include shell execution when users create commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with plugin commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers plugin command locations, plugin resources, scripts, agents, skills, and templates.

faq.question: How should I handle command arguments?
faq.answer: Document expected arguments, validate them early, and avoid direct shell interpolation.

faq.question: Why is allowed-tools important?
faq.answer: It limits what a command can access or execute during a Claude Code session.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing commands?
faq.answer: Review Bash usage, file access, argument validation, dependency assumptions, examples, and marketplace documentation.
